source_text: Quod ut breviter absolvatur, possibilitas est ad hoc solum excubans, ne homo vel in peccatum a quoquam impellatur, vel a peccato abstrahatur, voluntate captiva; quam non posse capi, si dedi ipsa noluerit, testatur fortitudo, cuius lacerti in contemptu dolorum et per Gentiles et per Christianos assidue claruerunt.
pass_a_gloss: Which that it may be briefly absolved, it is a possibility keeping watch unto this only, lest a human either be driven into sin by anyone, or be dragged away from sin, with the will captive; which cannot be captured, if it itself shall have been unwilling to give itself, courage testifies, whose arms in contempt of pains have shone continually both through Gentiles and through Christians.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: To state it briefly, it is a capacity whose sole watchful task is to ensure that no one is either driven into sin or dragged away from sin by someone else while the will is held captive. That the will cannot be captured unless it chooses to surrender is shown by courage, whose strength in despising pain has constantly shone forth among both pagans and Christians.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
